01_hook: Most people don't need another video telling them how to communicate.
They need a place to actually practice.
Because when the moment comes to speak, there is no script, no pause button, and no second take.
That's the problem Vocalis is built to solve.
02_intro: Vocalis is an AI-powered communication practice platform that turns speaking into a repeatable training loop.
You choose a topic, speak under a time constraint, get analyzed, turn that feedback into something practical, and then speak again.
The goal isn't another communication course.
03_onboarding: And Vocalis starts by making that practice personal.
You choose the communication skills you want to build, and then you're taken straight into the practice environment.
04_topics: There are multiple speaking categories, from everyday conversation and storytelling to interviews and deliberately unpredictable prompts.
The point is to make you think on your feet instead of rehearsing the same answer.
05_before_recording: Now I'm going to answer one completely unprepared question for 60 seconds.
No script. Just a real response.
06_feedback: This is where Vocalis becomes more than a recording tool.
The speech is transcribed and analyzed, and instead of giving me one meaningless confidence score, Vocalis breaks the response into useful communication signals.
I can see how I delivered the response, what worked, where I lost clarity, and what I should actually change on the next attempt.
The transcript also lets me inspect the response itself, including things like fillers, signposts, and key terms.
07_coach: And feedback doesn't have to stop at a report.
Vocalis also gives me a conversational voice coach, so I can ask follow-up questions, challenge the feedback, and practice with an actual AI conversation.
08_progress: The final piece is what turns a one-time demo into a habit.
Vocalis keeps the practice history and makes improvement visible over time.
So every session isn't an isolated conversation.
It becomes another data point in the process of getting better.
09_hackathon: We built something especially relevant to this hackathon.
Vocalis has a dedicated Hackathon Pitch Training Mode.
You can rehearse a one-minute elevator pitch, a three-minute standard pitch, or a full five-minute walkthrough.
The feedback is focused around things that actually matter in a pitch: the hook, problem and solution clarity, structure, evidence, feasibility, pacing, and delivery.
10_assemblyai: Under the hood, Vocalis is built around AssemblyAI's voice infrastructure.
We use AssemblyAI for speech recognition and transcription, and its Voice Agent technology powers the conversational coaching experience.
That voice data becomes the foundation for the analysis and feedback inside Vocalis.
So the AI isn't just sitting beside the product.
11_business: Our initial users are people who have something to say but don't get enough opportunities to practice saying it: students, interview candidates, founders, and hackathon teams.
From there, Vocalis can expand into premium coaching and organizational communication training.
make communication practice accessible, repeatable, measurable, and personalized.

mic_demo: Personally, I think mountains are better than beaches, although beaches are obviously great if your idea of relaxation is doing absolutely nothing.
The biggest difference for me is that mountains create a stronger sense of distance from everyday noise. You have changing terrain, colder air, and usually fewer distractions.
But I think the bigger reason is the sense of challenge. Even a short hike gives you a small goal, and reaching it makes the experience feel earned.
Beaches are great for switching off, but mountains are better for stepping back and thinking.
So if I had to choose one place to spend a week, I'd choose the mountains, partly for the scenery, but mostly because they make me slow down and actually be present.
